record.paper_title: Open questions in quarkonium and electromagnetic probes
record.original_question: What physics process produces the prompt intermediate-mass dimuon excess observed in indium-indium collisions after subtracting the expected Drell-Yan contribution and the contribution from correlated semi-muonic decays of charmed hadron pairs, and if the excess is thermal radiation, does it originate from a hadronic medium or from deconfined matter?

evidence.quote: It now remains to be understood what is the physics process responsible for this source of prompt dimuons. Maybe we are seeing thermal dimuons shining from a thermal medium (but, hadronic or deconfined?).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions of indium nuclei on indium nuclei at a beam energy of 158 GeV per nucleon, dimuon pairs are produced. After subtracting (i) the expected Drell–Yan contribution computed from perturbative QCD with standard parton distributions, and (ii) the contribution from correlated semi-muonic decays of pairs of charmed hadrons (D and anti-D mesons), a residual prompt excess of dimuons is observed in the intermediate-mass region 1 GeV < M_{μμ} < 3 GeV, where the excess pairs originate from the primary interaction vertex rather than from displaced decay vertices.

(a) Identify the physical production mechanism that accounts for this prompt intermediate-mass dimuon excess.

(b) Under the hypothesis that the excess is thermal electromagnetic radiation emitted from the hot, dense medium produced in the collision, determine whether the radiation originates predominantly from a hadronic (confined) phase, from a deconfined partonic phase (quark–gluon plasma), or from a combination of both, and quantify the relative contributions as a function of dimuon invariant mass and transverse momentum.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent NA60 analyses and theoretical interpretations indicate the prompt intermediate-mass excess is consistent with thermal radiation: below 1 GeV it is dominated by in-medium π+π− → ρ → μ+μ− annihilation with a strongly broadened ρ spectral function, while above 1 GeV the lack of significant radial flow and the spectral shape suggest a dominantly partonic (deconfined) emission source, consistent with parton–hadron duality. The qualitative picture is widely accepted, though the precise hadronic/partonic decomposition remains model-dependent.

status_evidence.title: NA60 results on thermal dimuons
status_evidence.snippet: The excess is consistent with a global interpretation as thermal radiation; for M>1 GeV the source appears dominantly partonic.
status_evidence.claim: Excess interpreted as thermal radiation with partonic-dominated source above 1 GeV.

status_evidence.title: Evidence for radial flow of thermal dileptons in high-energy nuclear collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Absence of significant radial flow for M>1 GeV suggests a dominantly partonic emission source.
status_evidence.claim: Intermediate-mass excess originates dominantly from deconfined matter.

status_evidence.title: Comprehensive interpretation of thermal dileptons at CERN SPS
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical interpretation supports thermal dilepton emission from both hadronic and partonic phases.
status_evidence.claim: Both hadronic and QGP contributions are needed, with QGP dominating at intermediate mass.
